children: Zimbabwe’s annual inflation rate rose for a second consecutive month to 4.3% in October 2026, its highest level since June, up from 3.7% in September.

The acceleration was driven primarily by housing and utilities (3.6% vs 0.8% in September), reflecting faster price increases for gas (25% vs 19.4%) and water supply and other dwelling-related services (17.6% vs. 16.9%).
Prices also rose faster for clothing and footwear (3.5% vs 2.6%).
Meanwhile, transportation inflation remained elevated at 12.9%, despite easing slightly from 13.2% in September, with fuel and lubricant prices rising by 15.3% (vs 15.4%).
Food and non-alcoholic beverage inflation slowed to 4.9% from 5.6%.
On a monthly basis, the CPI rose by 0.2%, after a 0.5% increase in the month before.

title: Zimbabwe Inflation Quickens to 4-Month High of 4.3%
